chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the woman who wears a bracelet and a hairpin on part of her arm, and she does not know if water flows beneath them or not. How should she act when she performs Wudu or Ghusl? He said: She should move them until water enters beneath them, or she should remove them.

And regarding the tight ring, if one does not know if water flows beneath it when performing Wudu or not, how should he act? He said: If he knows that water does not enter it, let him remove it when he performs Wudu.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing bracelets or tight rings during Islamic ablution (Wudu) and ritual bath (Ghusl)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'hijab al-ma'' (barrier to water) in ritual purity, distinguishing between uncertainty and certainty regarding water penetration under accessories. It reflects the Shia scholarly principle of resolving doubt by ensuring water reaches the skin, either through movement or removal, while mandating removal for items known to block water flow. This ruling underscores the importance of physical contact (ittisal) of water with the body parts during wudu and ghusl.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al-Amraky, from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the woman, upper her are bracelets, and the bracelets in one of her forearms is such that she does not know whether the water flows beneath it or not. How should she deal with it when she performs Ablution (Wudhu) or washes?’ Heasws said: ‘She should move it around until the water enters under it, or she should remove it’.

And about the tight ring, one does not know whether the water flows beneath it or not, how should one deal with it, heasws said: ‘If he knows that the water does not enter (under it), so let him take it out when he performs Ablution (Wudhu)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother, Musa ibn Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam) about a woman who wears a bracelet and there is bangle on her forearm and does not know if water reaches (her skin) under the bracelet, what should she do for Wudu’ or taking Ghusl (bath)? He (the Imam) said, ‘She must move them so that water reaches beneath or remove them.’
I then asked about a tight ring about which one is not certain if water reaches beneath when taking Wudu’.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If one knows that water does not reach beneath, one must remove it when taking Wudu’.’”
